title: Endpoint acceptance: regional fallback, backward compatibility, and launch checklist for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: capture the PRD and acceptance checklist for the hosted inference surface (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) with an explicit focus on backwards compatibility, regional failover behavior, and a minimal-risk go-live plan. This ticket consolidates requirements, acceptance criteria, and launch tasks that span API contract, runtime compatibility, observability, and operations runbooks.

Goals:
- Ensure existing customers (v1 clients) continue to function without code changes for standard request shapes.
- Define a clear compatibility matrix across four endpoint flavors (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank) and two delivery modes (streaming vs. non-streaming).
- Define regional failover behavior and SLOs when primary region is unreachable.
- Provide a launch checklist to hand off to SRE/Platform for final cutover and rollback criteria.

Scope (summary):
Included: API contract validation, schema compatibility wrappers, automated contract tests, synthetic traffic verification, canary rollout plan, error-code taxonomy, observability dashboards, and operator runbooks for regional fallback.
Excluded: SDK authoring (separate SDK release ticket), new model training or model architecture changes, UI/Console UX changes beyond showing endpoint status (handled by Console PM).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Backward compatibility: v1 request/response shapes remain accepted and unchanged for default routes. Any new fields are additive and ignored by v1 clients.
2) Contract tests: For each endpoint (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank) there is an automated contract test suite that runs in CI and a nightly contract check against the production routing layers.

3) Streaming & function-calling: Streaming behavior (chunk delimiting, event ordering) matches the published spec; function-calling tokens are emitted per spec. If streaming is unavailable in a region, non-streaming responses must be available as a graceful fallback and indicated via "streaming_available": false in the response metadata.

4) Embeddings stability: Vector dimensionality, normalization, and deterministic seeding for the curated embedding models must be documented and verified by unit tests; embedding length mismatch must return 400 with a typed error code EMBEDDING_DIMENSION_MISMATCH.

5) Rerank contract: Rerank endpoint accepts original ranking payload and returns stable scores within +/- 1e-4 for identical inputs across launches; scores susceptible to model changes must be flagged via model_version header.
6) Latency & throughput SLOs: p95 token latency for chat/completions <= 250ms in primary region under baseline synthetic load; regional-failover p95 <= 500ms under traffic-steering fallback.

7) Error taxonomy and observability: All endpoints must support the standardized error envelope (code, message, retriable) and emit taggable traces for request-id and routing decision; dashboards must show per-route error rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, and fallback percentage.

8) Canary & rollout: Canary must be run at 0.5% of production traffic for 24 hours with no customer-visible errors (error rate delta < 0.5% and latency regression < 10%); automatic rollback hook must be validated in staging.

9) Migration path: A header-based version negotiation (Accept-Inference-Version) must be supported for clients that explicitly want the newer schema; default behavior must be conservative so existing clients opt-in to new behavior.
10) Operational readiness: Runbooks for manual failover, capacity increase, and partial-region degradation must be authored, reviewed by SRE, and stored in the incident runbook repository.
out_of_scope: SDK releases and client-side migration guides (handled by Developer Experience)
Console UI changes beyond endpoint status indicators
Large refactor of the runtime kernel selection logic (engineering roadmap item)
decisions: D1: Keep default route conservative — do not change default request semantics to avoid breaking integrations. New behaviors exposed via version negotiation header only.
D2: Streaming will be gated in the first wave for EU-central and AP-south while we validate proxy stability; non-stream fallback will be required for those regions at launch.
D3: Rerank will not introduce scoring normalization changes at GA; any future normalization will be behind model_version flags and require a documented migration plan.
D4: Embeddings output will include explicit model_version and vector_schema metadata to make downstream consumers robust to future schema changes.

2026-03-02 — Design Review (Maya Ortiz): Confirmed that response metadata fields won't be surfaced in Console until after GA; approved the JSON contract sample.

notes: Risk: Compatibility wrapper CPU overhead may increase cost for high-throughput customers — mitigation: schedule a Dedicated capacity offer and cost analysis before GA.
Follow-ups: Post-GA plan to deprecate the legacy compatibility mode with a 6-month notice and an automated migration tool.
